For the Petitioner : Mr. Ajit Kumar Dubey, Advocate For the State : Mr. Suraj Verma, Addl.P.P ------
Order No.11/Dated- 14.05.2024 Heard learned counsel for the parties.

2. The instant criminal revision is directed against the judgment dated 11.04.2014 passed by learned Additional Sessions Judge-I, Palamau at Daltonganj in Criminal Appeal No. 29 of 2011, whereby and whereunder the appeal filed by the petitioner against the judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 03.03.2011 passed by learned Juvenile Justice Board, Palamau at Daltonganj in connection with Inquiry No.73 of 2011, Lesliganj P.S. Case No. 08 of 2009 corresponding to G.R.
Case No.261 of 2009, convicting the petitioner for the offence under Section 376 of the I.P.C. and was directed to be sent to the Special Home for a period of three years, has been dismissed.

entities.text: Additional Sessions Judge-I, Palamau at Daltonganj
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. The prosecution case was instituted on the basis of complaint petition filed by the informant that on 20.02.2009, the informant received a call from his wife reporting that petitioner had raped their four years' old daughter, Kalpana Kumari, causing bleeding.

The informant confirmed this upon returning home on 21.02.2009 and subsequently, filed a report with the Lesliganj police and accordingly, Lesliganj P.S. Case No.8 of 2009 corresponding to G.R. Case No.261 of 2009 was registered for the offence under Section 376 of the Indian Penal Code and the matter was inquired into by the Juvenile Justice Board, Palamau and petitioner was held guilty and instead of awarding any substantive sentence of imprisonment, he was directed to be sent to the Juvenile Special Home for the purpose of rehabilitation and reformation for a period of three years.
4. After completion of the investigation, police submitted charge- sheet on 15.05.2009 under Section Yaswant Kumar Singh S/O Late Pramod ... vs The State Of Jharkhand .... .... ...

1 376 of the I.P.C.
The cognizance of this case was taken by the learned C.J.M, Palamau on 22.05.2005 under the aforesaid sections.
The charge was framed against the accused person for the aforesaid section.

In the meantime, petitioner has taken the pleas of juvenile and made an application dated 30.03.2009 for ascertaining his age and upon his application vide order dated 06.05.2009, the petitioner was directed to be produced before Medical Board for ascertaining his age of the petitioner and thereafter he was declared juvenile and matter was referred to the Court of Juvenile Justice Board for disposal.
5.

The Juvenile Justice Board during course of inquiry and after considering the oral as well as documentary evidence adduced by the prosecution and after hearing the parties found the petitioner guilty for the offence under Section 376 of the I.P.C. and sentenced him as aforesaid.

6. The petitioner challenged the aforesaid order of the Juvenile Justice Board in Criminal Appeal No.29 of 2011 before the Additional Sessions Judge-I, Palamau at Daltonganj which was also dismissed vide order dated 11.04.2014 which has been assailed in this revision.

entities.text: Additional Sessions Judge-I, Palamau at Daltonganj
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 7. Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that petitioner was prosecuted for the offence under Section 376 of the Indian Penal Code for commission of rape of four years baby child of the informant.

Learned counsel for the petitioner has further submitted that at the time of alleged incident, the victim girl was alleged to be only four years' old and petitioner is close door neighbour of the informant.

There was cordial relationship between both the families and due to some dispute and differences, petitioner was falsely implicated in this case but unfortunately was found Juvenile in conflict with law through concurrent findings of the Courts below.
Petitioner is not going to the merits of the judgment but during pendency of the inquiry and the appeal, he has undergone one year's custody in the remand and has been sufficiently punished.

Petitioner has settled in his life and victim has also leading a normal life in the society, hence, petitioner may be directed to undergo the remand home already completed by the petitioner during the inquiry instead of maximum period of three years as awarded to him by the concerned Juvenile Board and affirmed by Appellate Court.

8. On the other hand, learned Additional Public Prosecutor has raised no objection as regard to aforesaid contentions advanced by the learned counsel for the petitioner and submitted that on merits, the revision is fit to be dismissed, but so far modification in sentence is concerned, in the factual aspect of the case, appropriate order may be passed.
9.

I have gone through the record of the case along with the impugned judgment of conviction and order of sentence passed by the learned trial court as well as judgment passed by the appellant court, it appears that the petitioner was found Juvenile in conflict with law through concurrent findings and he has also undergone about one year's custody in a remand home.
Now after lapse of 15 years from the alleged date of occurrence sending the petitioner in remand home or any other custody will not serve any useful purpose for the society.
The finding of fact of the court below appears to be correct legal and proper, requiring no interference on merits by way of this revision.

Yaswant Kumar Singh S/O Late Pramod ... vs The State Of Jharkhand .... .... ... on 14 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76998750/
2 10.

So far sentence awarded to the petitioner is concerned admittedly out of three years of Special Home, he has sustained substantial part of the imprisonment to the extent of about one year during course of trial/inquiry and during pendency of the appeal and this revision.
11. It appears that the date of alleged occurrence was of the year 2009 and more than 15 years has been passed from the alleged occurrence.
The petitioner has sustained agony of trial for the aforesaid period and also served sentence for one year.

12. Under the aforementioned circumstances, in the interest of justice, the imprisonment already undergone appears to be sufficient punishment for the offence committed by him, as more than 15 years has elapsed and it will amount to travesty.

13. In view of discussions and reasons, impugned judgment of the Court below is upheld on merits but with modification in sentence to the extent mentioned above i.e. petitioner is sentenced to go imprisonment for the period already undergone by him.
Accordingly, this revision is dismissed on merits with modification in the sentence.

14. Petitioner is on bail, as such, he shall be discharged from the liability of bail bond and sureties shall also be discharged.
15.
Let a copy of this order along with trial court record be sent to the concerned court forthwith for information and needful.

( Pradeep Kumar Srivastava, J.) Sachin Yaswant Kumar Singh S/O Late Pramod ... vs The State Of Jharkhand .... .... ... on 14 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76998750/
